# Destination right-sizing after cutover — facts

> Source-anchored units about Destination right-sizing after cutover: 14 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 14 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Destination right-sizing can include choosing a simpler topology during migration: MongoDB's live-migration configuration table includes sharded-to-replica-set migration, and Percona's ClusterSync presentation explicitly describes that path as right-sizing when sharding is no longer necessary. This is a migration-plan option, not evidence that an existing sharded destination can be converted merely by lowering its instance tier after cutover. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-10) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/live-migration.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://perconalive.com/2026-amsterdam/talks/zero-downtime-migration-with-percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For Atlas Core, storage auto-scaling increases capacity only; storage reduction is manual. Atlas can refuse a compute downgrade when the target tier cannot support the existing disk capacity or provisioned IOPS. Therefore, removing migration load does not by itself guarantee that the destination will return to a cheaper tier. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-storage.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md
- [statement] A January 2024 Atlas user reported that reducing logical data to roughly 200 GB left about 900 GB of storage and prevented an NVMe M60-to-M50 downgrade. This is a historical user report illustrating a storage-related downsizing obstacle, not a verified current product-wide limitation or a measured migration outcome. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/how-to-downsize-an-nvme-instance/263782 · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover
- [statement] Atlas Core refuses automatic compute downscaling when the target tier cannot support existing disk capacity or provisioned IOPS. Depending on the current and maximum tier, Atlas can disable downward auto-scaling or raise the minimum tier. Low CPU utilization alone therefore does not guarantee a lower tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-storage.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Size the steady-state destination from measured resource use and peak headroom, rather than copying source allocations or using CPU alone. MongoDB recommends monitoring CPU, WiredTiger cache, memory and IOPS; Microsoft's migration-sizing method independently uses CPU/memory, disk IOPS/throughput, performance percentiles and a comfort factor. Applying that general measurement method after MongoDB cutover is a synthesis, not an Atlas-specific Microsoft recommendation. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/target-right-sizing
- [statement] A defensible post-cutover sizing review uses observed workload demand rather than copying source allocations. MongoDB recommends reviewing CPU, WiredTiger cache, memory and IOPS over a rolling 30 days of normal use; Azure Migrate independently recommends performance-based target sizing using CPU, memory, disk IOPS and throughput. Applying the Azure method to Atlas is a methodological analogy, not an Atlas compatibility claim. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/target-right-sizing

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For Atlas pull live migration, MongoDB permits temporarily increasing the destination cluster size during migration and recommends post-migration performance tuning and sizing to minimize costs. Its general cost guidance also recommends downsizing persistently underutilized clusters. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/live-migration.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
- [statement] MongoDB's cost-saving guide recommends a rolling 30-day period of normal use for manual downsizing analysis. That is an observation recommendation, not a mandatory 30-day wait after every cutover; the reviewed migration guidance gives no fixed post-cutover waiting period. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/live-migration.md
- [statement] MongoDB's storage documentation says Atlas works around cloud-provider restrictions on in-place disk shrinking by provisioning replacement volumes and synchronizing data; it describes downtime on each node during synchronization. Treat shrinking excess migration storage as a planned rolling operation, without inferring that every application suffers a full-cluster outage. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover
- [statement] Migration-time compute allocation should not automatically become the permanent cost baseline: compare representative production demand with the destination tier after cutover. This is an inference from MongoDB's temporary migration sizing guidance and its recommendation to downsize consistently underutilized clusters; these sources do not establish a universal percentage saving. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/live-migration.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
- [statement] On Atlas Core, storage auto-scaling increases capacity only; reducing disk capacity requires a manual edit. Do not assume enabling auto-scaling will reverse migration-time disk growth after cutover. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-storage.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover
- [statement] For AWS-backed Atlas storage, a capacity decrease provisions new volumes and synchronizes data to them, with downtime on each affected node. It is not an in-place disk shrink. This statement does not imply that the entire replica set is unavailable throughout the operation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover
- [statement] IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB does not permit storage downscaling; its documented route after data reduction is backup and restore to a new deployment. This is an IBM destination constraint and must not be generalized to Atlas. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-resources-scaling · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover
- [statement] In Azure Migrate, performance-based assessments can use performance history, a chosen utilization percentile and a comfort factor to add safety headroom. This supports a demand-plus-headroom assessment method, but it does not demonstrate a MongoDB post-cutover outcome or prescribe Atlas tier settings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-07) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/target-right-sizing · keywords: Destination right-sizing after cutover
